It is the northernmost member of the [University of Massachusetts](University_of_Massachusetts "University of Massachusetts") public university system and has been [accredited](Higher_education_accreditation_in_the_United_States "Higher education accreditation in the United States") by the [New England Commission of Higher Education](New_England_Commission_of_Higher_Education "New England Commission of Higher Education") (NECHE) since 1975.[[5]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-5) With 1,110 faculty members and over 18,000 students, it is the largest university in the [Merrimack Valley](Merrimack_Valley "Merrimack Valley") and the second-largest public institution in the state.[[6]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-6) It is [classified](Carnegie_Classification_of_Institutions_of_Higher_Education "Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education") among "R2: Doctoral Universities – High research activity".[[7]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-7) The university offers 120 bachelor's degree, 43 master's degree, and 25 doctoral degree programs, including nationally recognized programs in engineering, criminal justice, education, music, science, and technology.[[8]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-report-8) The university is one of the few public universities in the United States to offer accredited undergraduate degrees in [meteorology](Meteorology "Meteorology"), [sound recording technology](Sound_recording_and_reproduction "Sound recording and reproduction"), [nuclear engineering](Nuclear_engineering "Nuclear engineering") and [plastics engineering](Plastics_engineering "Plastics engineering"). It was the first to offer a degree in music education. Academically, UMass Lowell is organized into six schools and colleges: the College of Fine Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences; the College of Education; the [Kennedy College of Sciences](Kennedy_College_of_Sciences "Kennedy College of Sciences"); the Francis College of Engineering; the [Manning School of Business](Manning_School_of_Business "Manning School of Business"); and the Zuckerberg College of Health Sciences.[[9]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-9) ## History The University of Massachusetts Lowell owes its origins to two institutions founded in the 1890s: [Lowell State College](Lowell_State_College "Lowell State College") on the south side of the [Merrimack River](Merrimack_River "Merrimack River") and [Lowell Technological Institute](Lowell_Technological_Institute "Lowell Technological Institute") on the north side. Each would follow its own path of expansion through the 20th century.[[10]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-Alloy-10) ### Lowell State College [Lowell State College](Lowell_State_College "Lowell State College") got its start as the Lowell Normal School, which was chartered in 1894 as a teacher-training institution for women. The 10th and final [normal school](Normal_school "Normal school") to be established in Massachusetts, it opened in 1898 with 108 students and five faculty members. The original classroom building opened the next year at the corner of Broadway and Wilder streets, and quickly became a landmark in the city.[[11]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-11) Designed by local firm Stickney & Austin, it reflects the fashion of the time: high-style [Beaux Arts](Beaux-arts_architecture "Beaux-arts architecture") with classical symmetry, arches, cast-iron lampposts and yellow brick. Its design was influenced in part by [Lowell High School](Lowell_High_School_(Massachusetts) "Lowell High School (Massachusetts)"), which was also designed by Lowell native [Frederick W. Stickney](Frederick_W._Stickney "Frederick W. Stickney"). Frank Coburn, for whom the hall was later named, served as the school's first principal until 1908.[[12]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-LowerMerrimack-12) After being threatened with closure during the Great Depression, school administrators rallied local support to help keep it open. A delegation of prominent individuals representing Lowell's powerful interest groups traveled to Boston and convinced state officials of the school's importance. The result was that the school not only survived, but continued to grow and expand. In 1950, Dr. Daniel O'Leary assumed the presidency and initiated an ambitious building program. The physical plant of the campus expanded during post-war era from a single structure to a multi-building complex, forming an area now known as UMass Lowell's South Campus.[[13]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-Frank-13) As the demand for more qualified teachers grew, the legislature reorganized the Normal School into [Lowell State College](Lowell_State_College "Lowell State College") in 1960 with a curriculum that expanded beyond education to include baccalaureate degrees in other fields including nursing and music. Beginning in 1967, the college was authorized to confer two more degrees: Master of Education and Master of Music Education.[[14]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-14) ### Lowell Technological Institute Established in 1895 as the Lowell Textile School, the institution was founded to train technicians and managers for work in Lowell's booming textile industry. Modeled after the now-defunct [Polytechnic College of Pennsylvania](Polytechnic_College_of_Pennsylvania "Polytechnic College of Pennsylvania"), Lowell Textile was the combined effort of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts and corporations eager to form a school dedicated to textile education. Under the guidance of founder James T. Smith, Lowell Textile opened its doors in February 1897 in the upper floors of a downtown commercial block located on Middle Street. The school offered three-year training programs in cotton and wool manufacturing, design, textile chemistry and dyeing.[[15]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-NewYorkTimes1-15) In 1903, the school moved from downtown to its permanent location just northwest of the Merrimack River. The yellow brick mill-like Southwick Hall was dedicated to Royal and Dierexa Southwick. Grandparents of the wealthy businessman [Frederick Ayer](Frederick_Ayer "Frederick Ayer"), the Southwicks were and abolitionists who came to Lowell in the 1820s to help establish the Lowell Carpet Company. Ten years later, the school granted its first bachelor's degrees in textile dyeing and textile engineering.[[16]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-16) In 1953, President Martin Lydon expanded the curriculum to include programs in plastics, leather, paper and electronics technology, increased the liberal arts offerings and renamed the school the Lowell Technological Institute.[[17]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-Frank2012-17) He moved the institute decisively toward general engineering, setting up a bachelor's program in 1956. The textile program was closed in 1971, reflecting the closure of most of the mills in the city.[[18]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-history-en-18) ### University of Lowell In 1972, a feasibility study was conducted on merging Lowell State College with Lowell Technological Institute.[[19]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-Study-19) Lowell State and Lowell Tech merged in 1975 as the University of Lowell. Durgin Hall, with its 1000-seat performance venue, was dedicated as the home of the Music Department.[[20]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-20) The Manning School of Business (then the College of Management Science) was accredited.[[21]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-21) The College of Education became certified to offer a doctorate in education (Ed.D.).[[22]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-22) The College of Health Professions (now the Zuckerberg College of Health Sciences) was established.[[23]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-23) Enrollment increased 58% by 1985.[[24]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-24) ### Merger with University of Massachusetts In 1991, the Lowell campus joined the University of Massachusetts system under its current name.[[25]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-25) Under Chapter 142, the UMass system was restructured to combine the [Amherst](UMass_Amherst "UMass Amherst"), [Boston](UMass_Boston "UMass Boston"), and [Worcester](UMass_Worcester "UMass Worcester") campuses with the University of Lowell and [Southeastern Massachusetts University](Southeastern_Massachusetts_University "Southeastern Massachusetts University") (now [UMass Dartmouth](UMass_Dartmouth "UMass Dartmouth")).[[26]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-26) ### Recent developments In 2019, a sexual harassment complaint against Associate Dean Oliver Ibe was settled by the university. The complaint was from a younger female staff member in 2017. Ibe's title of associate dean was removed and he returned to the faculty despite a petition from faculty and staff to have him removed from the campus.[[27]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-27)[[28]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-28)[[29]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-29) He retired the following year.[[30]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-30) ## Campus UMass Lowell is the second-largest campus in the University of Massachusetts system, and has three campus clusters: North, South, and East. The university's main facilities are located in [Lowell, Massachusetts](Lowell%2C_Massachusetts "Lowell, Massachusetts"), 25 miles (40 km) northwest of on both sides of the [Merrimack River](Merrimack_River "Merrimack River"). Between 2013 and 2018, the university increased student housing by more than 2,500 beds,[[31]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-31) including opening three new residence halls in 2013, 2015, and 2017. In fall 2021, thirty-five percent of undergraduates lived in university–owned, operated, or affiliated housing, including sixty-one percent of first year students.[[32]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-32) ## Organization and administration The university is governed by a six-member executive cabinet, including and led by the chancellor. The current chancellor is Julie Chen, who was appointed in May 2022.[[33]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-33) [Marty Meehan](Marty_Meehan "Marty Meehan"), former UMass Lowell Chancellor, is currently the president of the entire University of Massachusetts system. He assumed office in July 2015 after serving as the chancellor since September 2007.[[34]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-34)[[35]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-35)[[36]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-:0-36) ## Academics The University of Massachusetts Lowell has an acceptance rate of 72 percent,[[37]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-usnews-37) a freshman retention rate of 85 percent, and a graduation rate of 63 percent. In 2016, 87% of first-year students rated their overall educational experience as "good" or "excellent".[[8]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-report-8) The average combined SAT score (Critical Reading and Math) for incoming freshmen for fall 2018 was 1233, up nearly 150 points since fall 2010, and the average entering GPA was a 3.60, up from 3.18 in fall 2010.[[8]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-report-8) 47% of undergraduate classes had 20 students or fewer in the fall 2018 semester. In 2018 UMass awarded a total of 2,798 Bachelor's, 1,102 Master's and 122 Doctoral degrees.[[8]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-report-8) ### Tuition and fees The 2018-2019 annual tuition and fees for undergraduates were $15,180 (In State), $26,441 (New England Regional & Proximity) and $32,827 (Out of State). Graduate tuitions were $15,060, $22,871 and $26,840 respectively. As of the 2020–2021 school year the annual tuition and fees for undergraduates students are as follows, $15,698 (in state), $27,238 (New England/proximity), $33,624 (out of state), and lastly $36,525 (International). Graduate tuitions were $15,210, $23,021, $26,990, and $29,841 respectively.[[38]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-38)[[39]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-39) ### Online programs The university offers various courses online; in 2018, it had a total online-enrollment of 30,932 which was an increase of 7.4% compared to 2017. Total revenue from online classes in 2018 was $39.1 million.[[8]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-report-8) ### Colleges #### Francis College of Engineering The Francis College of Engineering is named after [James B. Francis](James_B._Francis "James B. Francis"), a hydraulic engineer who began his career in Lowell during the [Industrial Revolution](Industrial_Revolution "Industrial Revolution").[[18]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-history-en-18) The college is home to nearly 150 full-time faculty members and 14 research centers, and is fully accredited by .[[40]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-40) The college is ranked No. 118 by [U.S. News & World Report](U.S._News_%26_World_Report "U.S. News & World Report").[[41]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-usnews-grad-41) UMass Lowell has a [radiation laboratory](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell_Radiation_Laboratory "University of Massachusetts Lowell Radiation Laboratory") that provides students with real-world experience in [particle physics](Particle_physics "Particle physics"), [nuclear engineering](Nuclear_engineering "Nuclear engineering") and [health physics](Health_physics "Health physics"). The UMass Lowell Baseball Research Center is associated with the College of Engineering. The facility, first funded in 1998, is the official testing center for [Major League Baseball](Major_League_Baseball "Major League Baseball"), testing [bats](Baseball_bat "Baseball bat") and [baseballs](Baseball_(ball) "Baseball (ball)"). Those conducting research through the center include mechanical engineering faculty and a full-time staff engineer, and six to 12 student laboratory assistants.[[42]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-42) #### Zuckerberg College of Health Sciences The Roy J. Zuckerberg College of Health Sciences includes the Solomont School of Nursing, elevated from a department as of June 1, 2013. The college has more than 2,100 undergraduate students, 409 graduate students, 82 faculty members and six research centers.[[43]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-43) The college offers seven degree and certificate programs, including the only doctorate of [physical therapy](Physical_therapy "Physical therapy") (DPT) degree program offered by a public institution in Massachusetts. It also offers the only graduate degrees in pharmaceutical sciences at a public institution in the Commonwealth. The graduate nursing program is ranked No. 156 in the nation while the graduate physical therapy program is ranked No. 101, according to [U.S. News & World Report](U.S._News_%26_World_Report "U.S. News & World Report").[[41]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-usnews-grad-41) #### College of Fine Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences The College of Fine Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences includes the School of Criminology and Justice Studies, as well as signature programs including sound recording technology, music business, peace and conflict studies, security studies and more. The College of Fine Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences is the largest college at UMass Lowell and offers 24 undergraduate and graduate degree programs and houses seven centers and institutes, including the Kerouac Center for Public Humanities, named for writer [Jack Kerouac](Jack_Kerouac "Jack Kerouac"), a Lowell native.[[44]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-44) #### School of Education The School of Education offers bachelor's, master's and doctoral degree programs. The school includes 13 tenure-track faculty members and four clinical faculty members. The school has a 100 percent pass rate on the Massachusetts Tests for Educator Licensure. The online graduate education program is ranked No. 16 in the nation by [U.S. News & World Report](U.S._News_%26_World_Report "U.S. News & World Report").[[45]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-45) #### William J. and John F. Kennedy College of Sciences The [William J. and John F. Kennedy College of Sciences](William_J._and_John_F._Kennedy_College_of_Sciences "William J. and John F. Kennedy College of Sciences") has six departments: Biological Sciences; Chemistry; Computer Science; Environmental, Earth and Atmospheric Sciences; Mathematical Sciences; and Physics and Applied Physics.[[46]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-46) Originally the **UMass Lowell College of Sciences**, the college was renamed in honor of two alumni, John F. Kennedy '70 and William J. Kennedy '54, in 2015 (unrelated to the [political family](Kennedy_family "Kennedy family")).[[47]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-47) Research centers associated with the college include the New England Robotics Validation and Testing Center (NERVE), one of the nation's premier [robotics](Robotics "Robotics") research, testing and training facilities.[[48]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-48) Computer Science professor and NERVE director [Holly Yanco](Holly_Yanco "Holly Yanco") is currently collaborating with [Northeastern University](Northeastern_University "Northeastern University") professors Taskin Padir and Robert Platt in developing NASA's Valkyrie robot to research advancements in cutting-edge humanoid robotics.[[49]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-49) The graduate chemistry program is ranked No. 145 and the graduate physics program is ranked No. 124 in the nation by U.S. News & World Report.[[41]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-usnews-grad-41) #### Manning School of Business The [Manning School of Business](Manning_School_of_Business "Manning School of Business") is named after Robert J. Manning, the [chairman](Chairman "Chairman") and of [MFS Investment Management](MFS_Investment_Management "MFS Investment Management").[[50]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-50) The school was named after Manning, a 1984 graduate of UMass Lowell, after he and his wife donated $5 million to the university.[[51]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-51) The Manning School of Business consists of five departments: Accounting, Finance, Management, MEI (Marketing, Entrepreneurship, and Innovation), and OIS (Operations and Information Systems). The school offers Bachelor's, Master's, and PhD level degrees. ### Research Total R&D expenditure was $92.2 million in 2020.[[3]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-uml.edu-3) Many of the research and development opportunities include Working in a campus research lab, helping a community organization, conducting reviews of program-related scholarship, or working on a business or marketing plan for a local start-up.[[36]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-:0-36) Research can be done on anything, whether it is testing composite materials to advancing cyber security. #### Research Centers - Center for Advanced Manufacturing of Polymers and Soft Materials - Center for Advanced Materials - Center for Asian American Studies[[52]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-52) - Center for Population Health - Center for Program Evaluation - Center for the Promotion of Health in the New England Workplace - Center for Terrorism & Security Studies (CTSS),[[53]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-53) founded by [James J.F. [University Ranking by Academic Performance](University_Ranking_by_Academic_Performance "University Ranking by Academic Performance") for 2019-2020 ranks the university as No. 197 in the country.[[76]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-76) UMass Lowell is [accredited](Higher_education_accreditation_in_the_United_States "Higher education accreditation in the United States") by the [New England Commission of Higher Education](New_England_Commission_of_Higher_Education "New England Commission of Higher Education").[[77]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-77) UMass Lowell is known for having one of the highest returns on investment (ROI) in the country for its graduates. ranked UMass Lowell as the 10th best value among all universities and colleges nationwide for 2013 and fourth-best value among non-military academies.[[78]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-forbes.com-78) UMass Lowell is one of just 75 institutions in the nation whose graduates have a 30-year net ROI of more than $1 million. In 2013, Business Insider named UMass Lowell as the "Most Underrated College in America". The 2015 edition has named UMass Lowell as the second-most underrated college in the U.S. behind .[[80]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-80)[[81]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-81) ## Student life ### Student body Total enrollment for the 2019–2020 academic year is 18,338, including 2,481 students in online and continuing education.[[8]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-report-8) in the following academic year about 18,400 students enrolled in the university this fall, making the largest student body enrolled.[[82]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-82) In-state enrollment represents 88.3 percent of undergraduates and 58.4 percent of graduate students. International students make up 3.5 percent of the undergraduate population and 16.2 percent of the graduate population. Students of color represent 36 percent of the total undergraduate population and 25 percent of the graduate population. The male-female ratio for undergraduates in 2018 was 61/39.[[8]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-report-8) Total enrollment has increased 50 percent since 2007. ### Student activities UMass Lowell has more than 250 student-run organizations.[[83]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-83) #### Greek life Greek life was banned from the university campus after a hazing in 1987, where a student suffered overheating when left with a sleeping bag over his head near a space heater. Greek life was returned to the campus in 2012.[[84]](University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell#cite_note-84) ### Athletics Main article: [UMass Lowell River Hawks](UMass_Lowell_River_Hawks "UMass Lowell River Hawks") UMass Lowell athletic teams compete in a variety of men's and women's sports in [Division I](NCAA_Division_I "NCAA Division I"). Men's sports include [baseball](UMass_Lowell_River_Hawks_baseball "UMass Lowell River Hawks baseball"), [basketball](UMass_Lowell_River_Hawks_men's_basketball "UMass Lowell River Hawks men's basketball"), [cross country](Cross_country_running "Cross country running"), [ice hockey](UMass_Lowell_River_Hawks_men's_ice_hockey "UMass Lowell River Hawks men's ice hockey"), [lacrosse](Lacrosse "Lacrosse"), [track and field](Track_and_field "Track and field"), and [soccer](UMass_Lowell_River_Hawks_men's_soccer "UMass Lowell River Hawks men's soccer"). Women's sports are [basketball](UMass_Lowell_River_Hawks_women's_basketball "UMass Lowell River Hawks women's basketball"), cross country, lacrosse, track and field, [field hockey](Field_hockey "Field hockey"), soccer, and [softball](Softball "Softball"). As of July 1, 2013, 14 of UMass Lowell's [Division II](NCAA_Division_II "NCAA Division II") teams moved up to Division I, joining the [America East Conference](America_East_Conference "America East Conference"). The River Hawks, with the exception of men's ice hockey, previously competed in the [Northeast-10 Conference](Northeast-10_Conference "Northeast-10 Conference") at the Division II level.
